findings.evidence: '6. **Follow-up.** When the user asks a follow-up about a finished run, Gemini CLI can continue the earlier session: `gemini --resume latest` ... Sources: [CLI reference](...), [session management](...).' One numbered step packs a decision, two command forms, a doc caveat and source links into a single paragraph.
findings.fix: Split step 6 into a short decision: (a) interactive resume command for the user's terminal; (b) otherwise a new headless run that restates the accepted findings. Move the 'checked 2026-11-07' caveat and the source links to the Sources list under Gotchas. Keep all the content.

findings.evidence: Negatives such as 'write a Python script to scan our repository' and 'make a small code change in this repository yourself' share no Gemini, second-opinion or big-context concept with the skill, so they do not test the description's boundary.
findings.fix: Replace the two weak negatives with near-misses, for example 'use gemini to refactor src/auth and apply the changes' (Gemini implementing changes, which the description excludes) and 'set up a GitHub Action that calls Gemini on every PR' (CI integration, not a CLI review).

findings.evidence: 'For a background run, record the `timeout` PID and wait on it' plus `... & pid=$!` / `wait "$pid"`. The 300 s or 900 s budget can exceed a harness tool call's own timeout, which can kill the shell before `timeout` reports 124. A `$pid` set in one tool call is also gone in the next, yet references/troubleshooting.md depends on it.
findings.fix: Add to step 3: when the harness limits tool-call duration below the budget, launch with the harness's background-run option, or write the PID to a file (`echo $! > gemini.pid`). Then poll with `kill -0 "$(cat gemini.pid)"` and read gemini-review.log, instead of a blocking `wait`. Point troubleshooting.md at the saved PID file.

findings.evidence: Line 14: 'Use 900 for a >200k-token scope'. Line 68: 'A scope well over 200k tokens: split it by area (one directory or document group per run)'. 'Well over' has no threshold, so a 350k scope (the big-scope-budget eval) could go either way: one 900 s run or a split.
findings.fix: Give a concrete cut-off, for example: '>200k up to ~500k tokens: one run with the 900 s budget; above that, or when a 900 s run exits 124: split by area, one run per directory or document group, then merge the verified findings.'
